subject: dance
intro: Dance leads to performing and making work for the stage, and just as much to teaching in studios and schools, community recreation programmes and the production roles that put movement in front of an audience.

roles.title: Dancers
roles.entry: No formal education required; years of dance training
roles.what: Perform choreography on stage and screen: rehearse daily to build technique, audition for companies and productions, memorise and interpret movement, and adapt performances to directors' notes and tour schedules.
roles.where: Unit 1's physical, technical and expressive skills with safe dance practice and anatomy, and the anthology's set works, are the repertoire and conditioning a performing career runs on.

roles.title: Choreographers
roles.entry: Bachelor's degree in dance is common
roles.what: Create dance: generate movement from a stimulus, structure it into works, audition and rehearse dancers, revise material in the studio, and set choreography for companies, musicals, film and music video.
roles.where: Unit 2's stimulus, intent, choreographic devices and structuring, and unit 6's working with dancers, rehearsal and evaluation, are literally this job's process as the course teaches it.

roles.title: Self-Enrichment Teachers
roles.what: Teach for enjoyment rather than qualification: run studio classes in dance and movement for children and adults, plan progressive class content, correct technique, and stage showcases for family and community audiences.
roles.where: The performance-technique unit, safe dance practice, and the appreciation vocabulary for actions, dynamics and space are exactly what a studio teacher breaks down for beginners.

roles.title: Art, Drama, and Music Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach dance and the performing arts at universities: deliver technique and choreography studios, lecture on dance history and appreciation, direct productions, and publish or present research on the art form.
roles.where: Unit 5's dance history and contexts and unit 8's critical writing, alongside technique and choreography, are the syllabus strands university dance programmes are built around.

roles.title: Recreation Workers
roles.what: Organise activities for communities: plan and lead dance, movement and creative sessions at recreation centres, camps and care facilities, adapt activities to participants' needs, and keep programmes safe and welcoming.
roles.where: The choreographic-craft units scaled to community settings — simple stimulus-led tasks, group structuring, safe practice — match the movement programming this role leads.
